manufacturer: Scott Reagent (cobalt thiocyanate) — Standard forensic spot test
validationStatus: Prototype — colour regions from UNODC ST/NAR/42 (2013) Table 2, Scott (1973) J Forensic Sci, and Cole (2001) Microgram. Blue colouration indicates cocaine/crack cocaine presumptively. Not a validated diagnostic instrument.

referenceCard.description: Software-rendered 8-patch digital reference card displayed on-screen.
referenceCard.printNotes: No printing required. Display on a second device beside the sample.

reactionWindow.observationNotes: Scott is a two-step test. Capture after both reagent additions and the final blue colour has stabilised (approx 60 seconds).

captureInstructions: Step 1: Add 5 drops of Solution A (cobalt thiocyanate) to a small sample. Blue = possibly cocaine.
Step 2: Add 5 drops of Solution B (HCl). Blue colour persists if cocaine present; turns pink if not.
Step 3: Add 5 drops of Solution C (CHCl3 layer). Blue organic layer = presumptive positive for cocaine.
Wait ~60 seconds after final step for colour to stabilise.
Display the Digital Reference Card on a second device beside the sample.
Frame both the reaction area and the digital card within their guides. Press CAPTURE.
safetyNotes: Scott reagent contains hydrochloric acid and chloroform. Work in a ventilated area with PPE.
Chloroform is a suspected carcinogen. Minimise exposure and dispose per chemical waste rules.
Blue colouration is presumptive for cocaine/crack cocaine only. Many other substances give false positives.
